subject: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off
body:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

Marcus/Kevin — looping you in for security sign-off on the Private VPC Terraform modules (alpha).

We need an explicit “secure-by-default” position for:
- Security groups baseline (least privilege + default deny)
- VPC Flow Logs + routing/retention
- Exception handling (what can be opted out of, and how)

Confluence review doc (current working version):
confluence://security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/vpc-terraform-alpha-secure-defaults-review

Key questions we need answered by EOD Wed:
1) Can Flow Logs be default-enabled (with an explicit opt-out variable) for alpha?
2) What minimum retention do we require if using CloudWatch Logs?
3) Any required changes to the SG baseline before we can call this “secure defaults approved”?

Attachment: Terraform-secure-defaults-signoff-checklist-alpha-v2.pdf

If you can reply with “approved” + any blocking deltas, Irene can prioritize the changes in the next PR batch.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference


---

From: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 11:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

Reviewed the Confluence page + checklist.

Answers/requirements from my side:

1) Flow Logs default-enabled
- Yes, default should be enabled.
- Opt-out is OK only if it is explicit (enable_vpc_flow_logs = false) and the README calls it out as “reduced auditability” + we capture it as an “exception” in the deployment checklist.
- The module should support CloudWatch Logs and S3 destinations (aligning with the audit logging guidance):
  confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/vpc-flow-logs-and-central-log-routing-guidance

2) CloudWatch retention
- Minimum 90 days for alpha. Preferred 180 days.
- If we ship defaults, set 90 and allow override upwards.

3) SG baseline
- Blocker: avoid “0.0.0.0/0” ingress anywhere except where explicitly required AND documented (I did not see a required case).
- Egress: I’m OK with “allow all egress” as alpha default *only* if (a) endpoints are enabled by default for ECR/S3/Logs and (b) the README strongly recommends restricting egress and provides an example.
- Add input validation for custom port overrides (no opening broad ranges accidentally). If PR-246 already does this, great.

4) Exception handling
- We need a standard section in README: “Exceptions and risk acceptance” with (a) what toggles are available, (b) why they’re risky, and (c) who needs to sign off. It can be lightweight for alpha but must exist.

Not a blocker but requested: ensure log group encryption story is clear (KMS optional). If KMS not supported in alpha, call it out.

-Kevin


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 12:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

+1 to Kevin’s notes.

Security sign-off (conditional):
- APPROVE once Flow Logs are default-enabled + CW retention default is set to >= 90 days.
- APPROVE once README includes explicit exception language + points to the Confluence security review page.

One additional blocker from my side:
- Checkov/tflint suppressions must require a documented reason + reference (ticket id). No blanket suppressions in-module.

If those three items land, I’m comfortable calling it “secure defaults reviewed/approved for alpha”.

Marcus


---

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 2:18 PM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

Thanks — this is actionable.

Plan for implementation (unless Security objects):

Flow Logs:
- Make enable_flow_logs default true in the wrapper (redwood-private-vpc) and the baseline module.
- CloudWatch Logs as default sink, with retention default = 90d.
- Support S3 destination as option (already in PR-245, we’ll ensure it’s wired in wrapper + README).
- KMS: We can expose kms_key_arn for CW log group encryption. If that’s too much for alpha, we’ll at least document and ensure it can be added without breaking changes.

SG:
- Confirm no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rules in baseline.
- Keep allow-all egress for alpha baseline BUT add “restricted egress” example in docs, and recommend private endpoints (ECR/S3/Logs/STS) for locked-down environments.

Exceptions:
- Add README section: “Risk/Exceptions” with explicit opt-outs and required sign-off (Security + Product).

Static checks:
- No blanket suppressions. We’ll require a variable/toggle? (Probably not.) Instead, any suppressions in CI will be explicit in the pipeline and tied to a ticket.

I’ll coordinate PRs with Sahana on CI changes.

-Irene


---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 3:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

This looks good.

Request: can we land the “blocking” deltas by Thursday so we can keep the alpha gate on track?

For the exception language, please make it clear what is allowed for alpha pilots vs what triggers a formal exception (we’ve seen customers ask to disable flow logs / run with public egress by default).

Vivek


---

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 9:47 AM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

Adding one more constraint for the exception section (based on prior audits):

- If enable_flow_logs = false, the docs must state this impacts the customer’s ability to meet common audit logging expectations and that Redwood Support may require re-enabling for incident investigations.

Also, please make sure we explicitly call out where logs go (CW Logs vs S3) and who controls retention.

If Irene can confirm the changes are in-flight, I’ll update the Confluence page with “approved pending merge” language and tag Marcus for final yes.

Aisha


---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kevin Osei <kevin.osei@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 4:08 PM PST
Subject: Re: Terraform Private VPC modules (alpha) - secure defaults sign-off

Acknowledged on the added language.

Once Irene confirms:
- Flow logs default on (wrapper + baseline)
- CW retention default >= 90d
- Exceptions section added (incl. opt-out implications + support note)
- No blanket static-check suppressions (must reference ticket)

…then consider this signed off for alpha from Security.

Marcus
